posts.body:
Spent this past weekend at Texas Woman's University for the SWACUHO Student Staff Leadership Conference with our UT Dallas delegation!
One thing that stuck with me was a session on Southern hospitality. Making someone feel genuinely welcome changes the way a conversation goes, whether you're meeting someone for the first time, working with a team, or trying to resolve a disagreement. I left thinking more about how I listen and how I can make those conversations easier for the other person, too.
We also talked about planning as an ongoing process: figure out what you're trying to accomplish, make a plan, put it into practice, and look honestly at what worked and what didn't. Then use that to make the next attempt better. That's something I can bring into projects and everyday responsibilities, not just event planning.
I also had to get a photo at TWU's "Educate a Woman, Empower the World" wall. The women shaping our classrooms, communities, and workplaces deserve recognition, support, and room to lead. That message felt especially fitting at a conference about leadership.
Huge thank you to Thomas Abbey, PhD, my building coordinator, along with everyone in our delegation for making the trip such a good time. Thank you to Miguel Najera and the TWU team for putting on an amazing event!
I learned a lot, met people from other campuses, and got some good practice putting myself out there and networking. And yes, Buc-ee made it into the group photos.

posts.excerpt: RescueMEsh won at HackUTD! I know this is late, but I'm still so excited about this past weekend!! Huge thank you to my teammates Alex S. Huang, Dersh Bhakta, and Yash Chavan for building this with me. RescueMEsh is a...
posts.body:
RescueMEsh won at HackUTD!
I know this is late, but I'm still so excited about this past weekend!!
Huge thank you to my teammates Alex S. Huang, Dersh Bhakta, and Yash Chavan for building this with me.
RescueMEsh is an emergency-reporting prototype for when cell service and internet go down. Your phone connects over Bluetooth to a small radio device, which sends an encrypted SOS over LoRa to a nearby hub. The idea is to get a request for help out without depending on a working cell tower.
At the hub, NVIDIA Nemotron helps organize incoming reports, flag urgent cases, and suggest how resources could be allocated. An operator can still review the original reports and override those suggestions. We also built a regional dashboard to model coordination between hubs instead of treating every location as its own isolated problem.
That meant putting together an iPhone app, radio firmware, 3D-printed cases, and the dashboards. There were a lot of cables.
The event was chaotic and just about everything ran late, but I'm not going to hate on free. Unfortunately, no corporate sponsors stopped by our table. Clearly they missed out.
Anyways, take a look at what we built:
https://lnkd.in/gHqBUjZD

posts.body:
I’ve redone my website again. I think I’m keeping this one!!!!
I keep changing it because I never really know what someone takes away from it. I know what I’m trying to say about myself, but does that actually come across when someone spends a minute looking? (Part of doing what I do is having your work and what you build constantly perceived and critiqued)
This time I went stupid simple. My projects, what they actually do, and my resume. Some portfolios get a little carried away (yes, I’m talking about you, WebGL warriors). I don't want to play a video game to learn about you (I don't end up learning about you). Typeset font. All in a lowkey, lo-fi, lo-tech way.
Obviously, I still left some Easter eggs.
In this day and age I have spent a lot of time getting good at using AI to code, regardless, finding random hidden things in video games was one of my favorite parts of playing them as a kid. So just to make sure I still got it I implemented a feature all by myself (I know so crazy), if you spam click my profile picture too quickly, it grows rocket boosters and flies off the page. Probably unnecessary, but that part makes me happy.
I think this version feels more like me. Hopefully I can leave it alone long enough for someone else to actually see it.
Take a look: https://abhikhur.com
And if you’re hiring, especially take a look. I’m studying computer science and mathematics at UT Dallas and looking for more software engineering and research opportunities. <333

posts.body: I’ve been working on GridironDEX, an interactive football reference and play-design tool I built because most football glossaries stop at definitions.  It now has 105 reviewed concepts covering formations, coverage, fronts, blocking, special teams, and more. The tactical mode lets you choose personnel, draw routes, test calls against randomized defensive looks, and play through full drives.  The interesting engineering problem was keeping the diagram, simulation, contact timing, ball movement, and outcome logic on one deterministic clock. I built it with React and TypeScript.  Try it here: https://gridiron-dex.com  #React #TypeScript #SportsAnalytics #SportsTechnology
